events_tag.title: Will knots flip bitcoin core by ___?
events_tag.description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, by December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET, the number of Bitcoin Knots nodes exceeds the number of Bitcoin Core nodes. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No.”

The resolution source for this market is https://coin.dance/nodes/all, specifically the “Bitcoin Nodes” chart.
Resolution will be based on the node counts displayed when hovering over each date for Bitcoin Core Nodes and Bitcoin Knots Nodes.

A data point for a given day will be considered finalized once data for the following day is published.

If the resolution source becomes permanently unavailable within this market’s timeframe and before resolution criteria are met, the market will resolve based on a reliable alternative source or public data consistent with the official Bitcoin node counts.

events_tag.title: Another S&P 500 Company buys Bitcoin by ___?
events_tag.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if any S&P 500 company announces between November 4, 12:00 PM ET, and November 30, 2025, 11:59 PM ET that they bought Bitcoin for the first time. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This announcement can pertain to a first purchase of Bitcoin outside of the timeframe of this market (e.g. if a qualifying company announces it made its first purchase of Bitcoin prior to this market's timeframe, but the announcement is made within the timeframe, this market will resolve to "Yes").

The primary resolution source will be official announcements from qualifying companies; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if MicroStrategy announces that it will file for bankruptcy or has filed for bankruptcy of any variety by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

An announcement will suffice for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of if or when the actual filing occurs.

The announcement must be made through any of their official or verified channels, as a recorded or written statement by their CEO, legal representation, or other individual or team which officially represents MicroStrategy.

A definitive consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

"MicroStrategy" refers to Strategy Inc (formerly MicroStrategy Incorporated; Nasdaq: MSTR), the parent company of the Strategy group, or any other entity that is controlled by, or is under common control with, Strategy Inc and that holds, directly or indirectly, all or substantially all of MicroStrategy's business and assets at the time of the filing or announcement. Unless named above, foreign entities, financing entities, special purpose vehicles, and entities used to separate specific legal liabilities will not qualify, even if they meet that test.

A filing for bankruptcy means a petition by an entity this market refers to (each, a "covered entity") under Chapter 7 or Chapter 11 of the United States Bankruptcy Code, or a bankruptcy case for a covered entity filed in a court outside the United States under that country's bankruptcy or insolvency law, including a court-appointed administration. A petition filed against a covered entity by its creditors will qualify only if the court enters an order for relief on that petition by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

An announcement must state that a covered entity has decided to file for bankruptcy, or has filed for bankruptcy. Statements that the company is considering, exploring, or open to bankruptcy, or that bankruptcy is one of several options, will not qualify.

A definitive consensus of credible reporting may be used to confirm that a qualifying announcement or filing occurred. Reports citing unnamed sources that a covered entity plans or is preparing to file will not qualify on their own.

Once a qualifying filing or announcement occurs, this market will resolve to "Yes" even if the petition is later withdrawn, dismissed, or converted, or the company later reverses its decision.

The following will not qualify on their own: a missed payment or other default on debt; a breach of a loan covenant; foreclosure or other enforcement action by creditors; a credit rating downgrade; a debt exchange or other restructuring agreed outside of court; the appointment of a receiver; and an assignment for the benefit of creditors.

If a covered entity stops existing because of a merger or similar transaction, it will no longer be a covered entity. If, after the merger, no covered entity remains, this market will resolve to "No". If the transaction only changes a covered entity's name, state of incorporation, or legal form, or places a new holding company over the same business, the resulting entity will be treated as that covered entity.

A filing occurs at the time recorded by the court. An announcement occurs at the time it is first published by a covered entity or its representative.

events_tag.title: Bitcoin more valuable than any company before 2027?
events_tag.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point between November 11, 2025 and December 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET, the market capitalization of Bitcoin (BTC) exceeds the market capitalization of the largest publicly traded company in the world. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No." 

Market cap values for both BTC and companies will be taken directly from Google Finance. If Google Finance is unavailable, a consensus of credible financial data providers will be used.

events_tag.title: Will a new country buy Bitcoin by...?
events_tag.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the government of any sovereign UN member state announces between November 13, 3:00 PM ET and December 31, 2025, 11:59 PM ET that they bought Bitcoin for the first time. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

This announcement can pertain to a first purchase of Bitcoin outside of the timeframe of this market (e.g. if a country announces it made its first purchase of Bitcoin prior to this market's timeframe, but the announcement is made within the timeframe, this market will resolve to "Yes").

A qualifying purchase requires a relevant country take direct custody over the Bitcoin they purchase. Buying into investment vehicles, ETFs, etc., which do not constitute a direct purchase of Bitcoin, will not qualify.

The primary resolution source will be official announcements from the governments of any purchasing UN member state, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

events_tag.title: Will Bitcoin replace SHA-256 before 2027?

events_tag.title: Bitcoin vs. Gold vs. S&P 500 in 2026
events_tag.description:
This market will resolve according to the asset which has the best performance in 2026 among Bitcoin, Gold, and the S&P 500 with performance measured as the percentage change in price during the year for each asset. 

The percentage change in price for Bitcoin will be calculated by comparing the "Close" price for the Binance 1 minute candle for BTC/USDT on January 1, 2026 12:00 AM ET to the "Close" price for the Binance 1 minute candle for BTC/USDT on December 31, 2026 11:59 PM ET.

The resolution source for Bitcoin will be Binance, specifically the BTC/USDT "Close" prices currently available at https://www.binance.com/en/trade/BTC_USDT in the chart with "1m" and "Candles" selected on the top bar and the mouse on the candle for the relevant minute (the “time tools” selection may be used to view historical candles).

The percentage change in Gold will be calculated by comparing the official Gold Continuous Contract (GC00) Close price for the last trading day in 2025 to the official Gold Continuous Contract (GC00) Close price for the last trading day in 2026, as reported by MarketWatch.

The resolution source for Gold will be MarketWatch, specifically the close values reported for Gold Continuous Contract (GC00) under “Historical Quotes” at https://www.marketwatch.com/investing/future/gc00.

The percentage change in the S&P 500 will be calculated by comparing the official S&P 500 Index (^SPX) Close price for the last trading day in 2025 to the official S&P 500 Index (^SPX) Close price for the last trading day in 2026, as reported by Yahoo Finance.

The resolution source for the S&P 500 will be Yahoo Finance, specifically the Close values published by Yahoo Finance for S&P 500 Index (^SPX) at https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5ESPX/history/.

If two or more listed assets have exactly the same performance for 2026, this market will resolve according to the asset whose name, as listed in the title of this market, comes first alphabetically (e.g. if Bitcoin and Gold tie, this market will resolve to Bitcoin).

Only closing prices will be used for all calculations; total return measures will not be applied.

If either of the relevant trading days are shortened, the official closing price published for that session will be used.

If any relevant day lacks a specified closing price, the last valid historical closing price offered by the resolution source will be used.

events_tag.title: Bitcoin quantum-resistant upgrade implemented in 2026?
events_tag.description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if, by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, a quantum-resistant protocol upgrade is activated on the Bitcoin mainnet. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

To qualify, the upgrade must satisfy all of the following:
- The upgrade must constitute a consensus-layer change to the Bitcoin protocol that is live and enforced on the Bitcoin mainnet by the deadline. Proposals, drafts, code releases, miner signaling, node adoption, or activation on testnets or alternative networks do not qualify on their own.
- The upgrade must enable the use of a post-quantum-secure signature scheme for standard Bitcoin transactions on the Bitcoin mainnet. The scheme must be intended to provide meaningful resistance against quantum attacks on transaction signing (e.g., attacks against ECDSA or successor schemes). Purely theoretical proposals, wallet-level changes, off-chain solutions, layer-2 systems, or other non-consensus-layer mitigations do not qualify.
- The upgrade must make such quantum-resistant transaction types valid under Bitcoin consensus rules and generally available for use on the Bitcoin mainnet, even if their use is optional or not yet widely adopted.

“Activated” means the upgrade has reached the point at which its rules are enforced on Bitcoin mainnet blocks under consensus rules, following any required activation thresholds or lock-in periods.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

events_tag.title: Quantum breaks Bitcoin by ___?
events_tag.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, by 11:59 PM ET on the date specified, a quantum computer has been publicly demonstrated to derive a valid private key corresponding to an existing Bitcoin address using a quantum algorithm, such that the derived key is sufficient to sign a valid transaction on the Bitcoin mainnet. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

To qualify, the demonstration must satisfy all of the following:

The private key must be derived from a real Bitcoin address whose corresponding public key has been revealed on the Bitcoin blockchain (for example, via a prior transaction). The address must use standard Bitcoin cryptography with no artificial weakening or modification.

The target address must be reasonably believed not to be controlled by the demonstrator. This may be established through credible reporting, prior attribution (such as a known exchange or historical address), or broad consensus among experts. 

The derivation must rely on a quantum computing method that provides a computational advantage for solving the elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem underlying Bitcoin’s ECDSA (e.g., Shor’s algorithm or a comparable quantum algorithm). Purely classical methods, side-channel attacks, or approaches where quantum computation does not play a material role in deriving the key do not qualify.

The derived private key must be shown to be valid by either signing and broadcasting a valid transaction from the target address on the Bitcoin mainnet, or by independent reproduction and confirmation by multiple credible third parties. The result must be widely accepted by the cryptographic research community as valid.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

events_tag.title: When will the Bitcoin halving occur?
events_tag.description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the next Bitcoin halving occurs by the date specified in the title, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The next Bitcoin halving refers to the mining of Bitcoin block 1,050,000, the block at which the Bitcoin network’s block subsidy is next scheduled to be reduced by half.

The resolution source is mempool.space (https://mempool.space), specifically the “Timestamp” value displayed on the page for block 1,050,000 once it has been mined, converted to Eastern Time. For an example of where the “Timestamp” value is displayed on a block’s page, see this earlier block: https://mempool.space/block/00000000000000000001e019fb455cb292d5ba5b41ebfad92ab4e0f378e83d25.

This market is based solely on the “Timestamp” value displayed on mempool.space for block 1,050,000, not on network propagation or observation times, data from third-party explorers, or unofficial sources.

If the resolution source becomes permanently unavailable within this market’s timeframe and before resolution criteria are met, the market will resolve based on a reliable alternative source, such as another Bitcoin block explorer, or public data consistent with the Bitcoin blockchain.

events_tag.title: US Treasury announces Bitcoin purchase by ___?
events_tag.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the US Department of the Treasury officially announces that it has purchased Bitcoin between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The announcement must clearly and unambiguously communicate a completed purchase of Bitcoin; statements that the Treasury intends, plans, or is authorized to purchase Bitcoin, including through legislation or an executive order, will not qualify. Bitcoin acquired through seizure, forfeiture, or other non-purchase means, and indirect exposure such as funds or ETFs, will not qualify.

An announcement will suffice for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether the announcement is later reversed or retracted, or whether the Bitcoin is subsequently sold.

A qualifying announcement must come from an official U.S. government source or an authorized U.S. government official acting in an official capacity, and must concern a purchase carried out by or on behalf of the Treasury. Qualifying sources include Treasury press releases, statements, websites, social media accounts, and Federal Register notices, as well as recorded or written statements by Treasury officials, the President, or the White House. For purposes of this market, the Treasury includes its bureaus and sub-bodies, such as the Bureau of the Fiscal Service, and any Treasury-authorized entity acting on its behalf.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the United States government; however, a definitive consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events_tag.title: Bitcoin green days week of October 26?
events_tag.description:
This market will resolve to the number of green days for Bitcoin (BTC/USDT) during the specified week.

Exactly one outcome in this market will resolve to “Yes”.

The week consists of the seven Binance 1-day candles beginning at 12:00 AM UTC on the specified date (Monday - Sunday). A day is a green day if the finalized "CHANGE" value displayed for its candle is equal to or greater than 0.00%.

A 1-day candle must be finalized before it is considered for this market (namely, once the next 1-day candle is published, the previous one is finalized).

This market will resolve once the first 1-day candle of the following week is published, finalizing the last candle of the specified week. If a candle is unavailable, this market will resolve according to the value as first displayed once data is again available, no later than the end of the second calendar day (ET) after the end of the specified week.

The resolution source for this market is Binance, specifically the BTC/USDT trading pair, with the chart settings on "1D" and "Candles" selected on the top bar: https://www.binance.com/en/trade/BTC_USDT

Please note that this market is about the price according to the Binance BTC/USDT trading pair, not according to any other sources, exchanges, or trading pairs.

events_tag.description:
This market will resolve according to the Bitcoin Hashprice Index value displayed for the specified week (the weekly datapoint beginning Monday, 12:00 AM UTC).

If the displayed value falls exactly on the boundary between two brackets, this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

Exactly one outcome in this market will resolve to "Yes".

The Bitcoin Hashprice Index value is the US dollar hashprice per petahash per second per day (USD per PH/s per day). To see the value, mouse over the datapoint for the specified week on the chart.

A weekly datapoint is considered finalized once the datapoint for the following week is published. At that point, the prior week's value is considered finalized.

This market will resolve once the weekly datapoint for the specified week is finalized. If the value is unavailable, this market will resolve according to the value as first displayed once data is again available, no later than the end of the second calendar day (ET) after the end of the specified week. If no value for the specified week is displayed by that time, this market will resolve to the lowest listed bracket. No substitute index or data provider will be used.

In case of obvious data integrity issues (i.e., erroneous data), the market may remain open until the end of the third calendar day (ET) after such data is first released to allow for corrections; this applies only to clerical or similar errors, not to Hashrate Index differing from other sources.

Revisions to the value displayed for the specified week made after that datapoint is finalized will not be considered for resolution.

The resolution source for this market is the Bitcoin Hashprice Index chart at https://data.hashrateindex.com/network-data/bitcoin-hashprice-index, with "USD" and "PH/s" selected and the chart period set to "ALL".

Please note that the outcome of this market depends solely on the Bitcoin Hashprice Index as displayed on Hashrate Index. Values from other data providers, independently calculated hashprice estimates, or other indexes will not be considered for the resolution of this market.

events_tag.title: How high will Bitcoin's fee share get in November?
events_tag.description:
This market will immediately resolve to "Yes" if the "Fees / Total block income (%)" value displayed for any day during the specified month on the Bitbo Fees Percent of Reward chart is equal to or greater than the listed percentage. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The value for a day is read by mousing over that day on the chart.

A daily datapoint is considered finalized once the datapoint for the following day is published. At that point, the prior day's value is considered finalized. Only finalized daily datapoints will be considered for the resolution of this market.

This market will resolve as soon as a finalized datapoint meets the listed percentage, or once the datapoint for the final day of the specified month is finalized. If any daily datapoint for the specified month remains unpublished 2 calendar days (ET) after the end of the month, this market will resolve based on the finalized datapoints published up to that point.

In case of obvious data integrity issues (i.e., erroneous data), the market may remain open until the end of the third calendar day (ET) after such data is first released to allow for corrections; this applies only to clerical or similar errors, not to Bitbo differing from other sources.

Otherwise, once a finalized datapoint has met or exceeded the listed percentage, this market will resolve to "Yes" regardless of subsequent revisions.

The resolution source for this market is the "Fees / Total block income (%)" series on the Bitbo Fees Percent of Reward chart at https://charts.bitbo.io/fees-percent-of-reward/.

Please note that the outcome of this market depends solely on the values displayed on Bitbo. Independently calculated fee-to-revenue ratios or values from other sources will not be considered for the resolution of this market.

events_tag.title: Bitcoin green days week of November 16?
events_tag.description:
This market will resolve to the number of green days for Bitcoin (BTC/USDT) during the specified week.

Exactly one outcome in this market will resolve to “Yes”.

The week consists of the seven Binance 1-day candles beginning at 12:00 AM UTC on the specified date (Monday - Sunday). A day is a green day if the finalized "CHANGE" value displayed for its candle is equal to or greater than 0.00%.

A 1-day candle must be finalized before it is considered for this market (namely, once the next 1-day candle is published, the previous one is finalized).

events_tag.title: Best performing coin: week of November 16?
events_tag.description:
This market will resolve according to the crypto asset with the best percentage performance for the specified week among the listed assets. If all listed assets decline for the week, the asset with the smallest decline is the best performer. If two or more listed assets are exactly tied for the best percentage performance, this market will resolve according to the tied asset whose listed name comes first in alphabetical order. Exactly one outcome in this market will resolve to "Yes".

The percentage performance for each asset is the finalized "CHANGE" value displayed for its Binance 1-week candle beginning at 12:00 AM UTC on the specified date. Values will be used exactly as published, without rounding; Binance reports "CHANGE" to 2 decimal places. Because HYPE does not have a Binance spot listing, Hyperliquid is measured using the Binance HYPEUSDT perpetual futures contract, with "Last Price" candles selected.

A 1-week candle must be finalized before it is considered for this market (namely, once the next 1-week candle is published, the previous one is finalized). An asset for which no finalized 1-week candle is published for the specified week — including due to a delisting or suspension of its listed trading pair — will not be considered for resolution. No substitute pair or source will be used.

This market will resolve once the specified week's candles are finalized. If any listed asset's candle is unfinalized at that time, this market will resolve according to the finalized candles published no later than the end of the second calendar day (ET) after the end of the specified week.

In case of obvious data integrity issues (i.e., erroneous data), the market may remain open until the end of the third calendar day (ET) after such data is first released to allow for corrections; this applies only to clerical or similar errors, not to Binance differing from other sources. This period may extend past the resolution deadline above.

The resolution source for this market is Binance, specifically the following trading pairs, with the chart settings on "1W" and "Candles" selected on the top bar:
Bitcoin: https://www.binance.com/en/trade/BTC_USDT

Dogecoin: https://www.binance.com/en/trade/DOGE_USDT
Ethereum: https://www.binance.com/en/trade/ETH_USDT
Hyperliquid: https://www.binance.com/en/futures/HYPEUSDT
Solana: https://www.binance.com/en/trade/SOL_USDT
XRP: https://www.binance.com/en/trade/XRP_USDT

events_tag.title: Best performing coin: week of November 23?
events_tag.description:
This market will resolve according to the crypto asset with the best percentage performance for the specified week among the listed assets. If all listed assets decline for the week, the asset with the smallest decline is the best performer. If two or more listed assets are exactly tied for the best percentage performance, this market will resolve according to the tied asset whose listed name comes first in alphabetical order. Exactly one outcome in this market will resolve to "Yes".

The percentage performance for each asset is the finalized "CHANGE" value displayed for its Binance 1-week candle beginning at 12:00 AM UTC on the specified date. Values will be used exactly as published, without rounding; Binance reports "CHANGE" to 2 decimal places. Because HYPE does not have a Binance spot listing, Hyperliquid is measured using the Binance HYPEUSDT perpetual futures contract, with "Last Price" candles selected.

A 1-week candle must be finalized before it is considered for this market (namely, once the next 1-week candle is published, the previous one is finalized). An asset for which no finalized 1-week candle is published for the specified week — including due to a delisting or suspension of its listed trading pair — will not be considered for resolution. No substitute pair or source will be used.

This market will resolve once the specified week's candles are finalized. If any listed asset's candle is unfinalized at that time, this market will resolve according to the finalized candles published no later than the end of the second calendar day (ET) after the end of the specified week.

In case of obvious data integrity issues (i.e., erroneous data), the market may remain open until the end of the third calendar day (ET) after such data is first released to allow for corrections; this applies only to clerical or similar errors, not to Binance differing from other sources. This period may extend past the resolution deadline above.

events_tag.title: Bitcoin hashprice: week of November 9?
events_tag.description:
This market will resolve according to the Bitcoin Hashprice Index value displayed for the specified week (the weekly datapoint beginning Monday, 12:00 AM UTC).

If the displayed value falls exactly on the boundary between two brackets, this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

Exactly one outcome in this market will resolve to "Yes".

The Bitcoin Hashprice Index value is the US dollar hashprice per petahash per second per day (USD per PH/s per day). To see the value, mouse over the datapoint for the specified week on the chart.

A weekly datapoint is considered finalized once the datapoint for the following week is published. At that point, the prior week's value is considered finalized.

This market will resolve once the weekly datapoint for the specified week is finalized. If the value is unavailable, this market will resolve according to the value as first displayed once data is again available, no later than the end of the second calendar day (ET) after the end of the specified week. If no value for the specified week is displayed by that time, this market will resolve to the lowest listed bracket. No substitute index or data provider will be used.

In case of obvious data integrity issues (i.e., erroneous data), the market may remain open until the end of the third calendar day (ET) after such data is first released to allow for corrections; this applies only to clerical or similar errors, not to Hashrate Index differing from other sources.

Revisions to the value displayed for the specified week made after that datapoint is finalized will not be considered for resolution.

The resolution source for this market is the Bitcoin Hashprice Index chart at https://data.hashrateindex.com/network-data/bitcoin-hashprice-index, with "USD" and "PH/s" selected and the chart period set to "ALL".

Please note that the outcome of this market depends solely on the Bitcoin Hashprice Index as displayed on Hashrate Index. Values from other data providers, independently calculated hashprice estimates, or other indexes will not be considered for the resolution of this market.

This market will resolve according to the Bitcoin Hashprice Index value displayed for the specified week (the weekly datapoint beginning Monday, 12:00 AM UTC).

If the displayed value falls exactly on the boundary between two brackets, this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

Exactly one outcome in this market will resolve to "Yes".

The Bitcoin Hashprice Index value is the US dollar hashprice per petahash per second per day (USD per PH/s per day). To see the value, mouse over the datapoint for the specified week on the chart.

A weekly datapoint is considered finalized once the datapoint for the following week is published. At that point, the prior week's value is considered finalized.

This market will resolve once the weekly datapoint for the specified week is finalized. If the value is unavailable, this market will resolve according to the value as first displayed once data is again available, no later than the end of the second calendar day (ET) after the end of the specified week. If no value for the specified week is displayed by that time, this market will resolve to the lowest listed bracket. No substitute index or data provider will be used.

In case of obvious data integrity issues (i.e., erroneous data), the market may remain open until the end of the third calendar day (ET) after such data is first released to allow for corrections; this applies only to clerical or similar errors, not to Hashrate Index differing from other sources.

Revisions to the value displayed for the specified week made after that datapoint is finalized will not be considered for resolution.

The resolution source for this market is the Bitcoin Hashprice Index chart at https://data.hashrateindex.com/network-data/bitcoin-hashprice-index, with "USD" and "PH/s" selected and the chart period set to "ALL".

Please note that the outcome of this market depends solely on the Bitcoin Hashprice Index as displayed on Hashrate Index. Values from other data providers, independently calculated hashprice estimates, or other indexes will not be considered for the resolution of this market.

events_tag.title: Bitcoin difficulty adjustment at block 977,760?
events_tag.description:
This market will resolve according to the Bitcoin difficulty adjustment that occurs at the specified block height. Block 977,760 is the next difficulty retarget height and is currently expected to be reached on or around November 29, 2026 (ET).

If the displayed percentage falls exactly on the boundary between two brackets, this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

Exactly one outcome in this market will resolve to "Yes".

The difficulty adjustment is the percentage change in Bitcoin network difficulty that takes effect at the specified block height, as displayed in the "Change" column of the Adjustments table on the mempool.space Mining Dashboard. A positive percentage is an "up" adjustment and a negative percentage is a "down" adjustment.

If mempool.space does not display the adjustment for the specified block height within 2 calendar days (ET) after that block height is reached, the adjustment percentage as shown by a consensus of credible block explorers will be used. If block 977,760 has not been reached by 11:59 PM ET on December 27, 2026, this market will resolve to the lowest listed bracket.

The resolution source for this market is the mempool.space Mining Dashboard at https://mempool.space/mining, specifically the "Change" column of the Adjustments table for the specified block height.

Please note that the outcome of this market depends solely on the difficulty adjustment percentage as displayed on mempool.space, or, where mempool.space does not display it as described above, the consensus of credible block explorers. Values from other sources will not otherwise be considered for the resolution of this market.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Metamask officially launches a token by June 30, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

The primary resolution source for this market will be information from Metamask, however a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

The token must be actively, publicly transferable and tradable to be considered a launch.

events_crypto.title: Will Satoshi move any Bitcoin in 2026?
events_crypto.description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if any wallet labeled as belonging to Satoshi Nakamoto on Arkham’s Intel Explorer shows an “Outflow” or “Swaps” transaction at any time between January 9, 2026, 1:00 PM ET and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

The resolution source for this market is Arkham’s Intel Explorer, specifically the entity page for Satoshi Nakamoto available at https://intel.arkm.com/explorer/entity/satoshi-nakamoto

If Arkham becomes permanently unavailable, this market will resolve based on a consensus of credible sources.

events_crypto.title: Bitcoin vs. Gold vs. S&P 500 in 2026
events_crypto.description:
This market will resolve according to the asset which has the best performance in 2026 among Bitcoin, Gold, and the S&P 500 with performance measured as the percentage change in price during the year for each asset. 

The percentage change in price for Bitcoin will be calculated by comparing the "Close" price for the Binance 1 minute candle for BTC/USDT on January 1, 2026 12:00 AM ET to the "Close" price for the Binance 1 minute candle for BTC/USDT on December 31, 2026 11:59 PM ET.

The resolution source for Bitcoin will be Binance, specifically the BTC/USDT "Close" prices currently available at https://www.binance.com/en/trade/BTC_USDT in the chart with "1m" and "Candles" selected on the top bar and the mouse on the candle for the relevant minute (the “time tools” selection may be used to view historical candles).

The percentage change in Gold will be calculated by comparing the official Gold Continuous Contract (GC00) Close price for the last trading day in 2025 to the official Gold Continuous Contract (GC00) Close price for the last trading day in 2026, as reported by MarketWatch.

The resolution source for Gold will be MarketWatch, specifically the close values reported for Gold Continuous Contract (GC00) under “Historical Quotes” at https://www.marketwatch.com/investing/future/gc00.

The percentage change in the S&P 500 will be calculated by comparing the official S&P 500 Index (^SPX) Close price for the last trading day in 2025 to the official S&P 500 Index (^SPX) Close price for the last trading day in 2026, as reported by Yahoo Finance.

The resolution source for the S&P 500 will be Yahoo Finance, specifically the Close values published by Yahoo Finance for S&P 500 Index (^SPX) at https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5ESPX/history/.

If two or more listed assets have exactly the same performance for 2026, this market will resolve according to the asset whose name, as listed in the title of this market, comes first alphabetically (e.g. if Bitcoin and Gold tie, this market will resolve to Bitcoin).

Only closing prices will be used for all calculations; total return measures will not be applied.

If either of the relevant trading days are shortened, the official closing price published for that session will be used.

If any relevant day lacks a specified closing price, the last valid historical closing price offered by the resolution source will be used.

events_crypto.title: Base FDV above ___ one day after launch?
events_crypto.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Fully Diluted Valuation of Base's governance token is greater than the value specified in the title 1 day after launch. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No."

The token must be actively, publicly transferable and tradable to be considered a launch.

The FDV will be determined using the total token supply multiplied by the token price.

"1 day after launch" is defined as 4:00 PM ET on the calendar day following launch. The resolution source for this market is the most liquid price source available. If Base doesn't launch a token by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

If it becomes impossible for a given month to have the highest percentage change in 2026, that outcome may resolve to “No” immediately.

markets.description:

events_crypto.title: Abstract FDV above ___ one day after launch?
events_crypto.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Fully Diluted Valuation of Abstract's governance token is greater than the value specified in the title 1 day after launch. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No."

The token must be actively, publicly transferable and tradable to be considered a launch.

The FDV will be determined using the total token supply multiplied by the token price.

"1 day after launch" is defined as 4:00 PM ET on the calendar day following launch. The resolution source for this market is the most liquid price source available. If Abstract doesn't launch a token by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

events_crypto.title: Which Senators will vote for the Clarity Act?
events_crypto.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed Senator votes "Yea" on the first Senate vote on final passage of crypto market structure legislation occurring before January 1, 2027. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For purposes of this market, "crypto market structure legislation" is defined identically to Polymarket's "Crypto Market Structure legislation becomes law in 2026?" market: https://polymarket.com/event/crypto-market-structure-legislation-becomes-law-in-2026-20260727223933088

The qualifying vote is the first vote on final passage of the bill in the full Senate - not a committee vote, and not a vote on a motion to proceed, a motion to invoke cloture, or an amendment.

This market will resolve to "No" if no qualifying vote occurs before January 1, 2027, or if the named Senator does not vote "Yea" on the qualifying vote for any reason - including voting "Nay," voting "Present," being absent, being paired, or no longer serving in the Senate at the time of the vote.

Once the vote has closed and the result has been announced, any subsequent request by the named Senator to add, remove, or change their vote will not be considered for purposes of this market, regardless of any change to the official vote tally.

This market will resolve according to official records of the U.S. Senate (http://senate.gov) and Library of Congress (http://congress.gov).

events_crypto.title: First to hit $1B FDV: ANSEM, CASHCAT, AI, or NET?
events_crypto.description:
This event will resolve to the first of the coins listed below to reach a fully diluted valuation equal to or greater than $1,000,000,000 at any point between the creation of this event and December 25, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. If no coin listed below reaches a fully diluted valuation of $1,000,000,000 or greater by that time, this event will resolve to "None".

Fully diluted valuation refers to the figure published by each coin's resolution source, shown as "Fully Diluted Valuation" on CoinGecko and as "FDV" on CoinMarketCap. Circulating supply market cap will not be used.

The coins in this event, and their resolution sources, are:

- Cash Cat (CASHCAT), Robinhood Chain 0x020bfc650a365f8bb26819deaabf3e21291018b4, CoinGecko, https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/cash-cat
- Artificial Inu (AI), Robinhood Chain 0x2E8c31162b855A2ffa90F6F8634643Ad6F111e18, CoinMarketCap, https://coinmarketcap.com/currencies/artificial-inu-ai/
- The Black Bull (ANSEM), Solana 9cRCn9rGT8V2imeM2BaKs13yhMEais3ruM3rPvTGpump, CoinGecko, https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/the-black-bull
- NetNet (NET), Robinhood Chain 0xca9c78dd337a67f6e0077f65f5e9218719d30edf, CoinGecko, https://www.coingecko.com/en/coins/netnet

A coin reaches the threshold at the first moment its fully diluted valuation, as displayed on its resolution source, is equal to or greater than $1,000,000,000. If two or more coins first reach the threshold within the same minute, the coin with the higher fully diluted valuation at that minute will be treated as first.

A momentary crossing qualifies, provided it is verifiable from the resolution source or from a consensus of credible reporting.

Each coin is judged solely against the source listed for it. Differences in methodology between CoinGecko and CoinMarketCap will not be adjusted for.

The primary resolution source for this event will be the source listed above for each coin; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used. If a resolution source becomes permanently unavailable or stops publishing data for a coin, that coin will resolve based on other credible and publicly verifiable sources.

events_crypto.title: SBF released from custody in 2026?
events_crypto.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Sam Bankman-Fried is released from custody by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If Sam Bankman-Fried is released but remains under house arrest, the market will still resolve to "Yes".

If Sam Bankman-Fried is released on parole, bond, or any other condition that results in them leaving state custody, the market will resolve to "Yes".

Transporting Sam Bankman-Fried to another location of custody (e.g., a different prison, court, or hospital within the correctional system) will not suffice to resolve this market to "Yes".

Temporary outings from prison for purposes such as testifying in court or before Congress, while still under the custody of correctional authorities, will not count as a release.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from government authorities or corrections departments; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

events_crypto.title: Consensys IPO closing market cap above ___ ?
events_crypto.description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the official closing price for Consensys’ market capitalization on its first trading day is above the value specified in the title. Otherwise, it will resolve to “No”.

If no IPO occurs by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “No”.

Market capitalization is defined as the total number of outstanding shares multiplied by the closing share price on the first trading day.

Resolution will be based on the primary exchange’s official listing page. In the event that the relevant figure is not displayed, another reliable source will be used.

In the event of an interruption in the course of the normal trading session on Consensys’s first day of trading (e.g., a circuit breaker or half-day), the market will resolve according to the official closing price of the abbreviated session. If no such official closing price is published, the market will resolve according to the next trading day on which an official closing price is published, treating that as the first day of trading.

markets.question: USDC depeg by December 31?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” immediately if all Pyth 1-minute candles for USDC-USD for any 24-hour period are below 98 cents, for candles between 27 Oct ’25 15:00 and 31 Dec ’26 23:59 ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No.”

Below 98 cents means all candles in the period have a final “High” price below 0.98000 (i.e., 0.97999 or lower). A 24-hour period of USDC below 98 cents that starts on the last day in 2026 will count.

The resolution source for this market is TradingView, specifically the USDC-USD “High” prices currently available at https://tradingview.com/chart/?symbol=PYTH%3AUSDCUSD with “1m” and “Candles” selected on the top bar. To see the “High” prices, mouse over particular candles and look at the value after “H” at the top of the chart.

Please note that this market is about the price according to Pyth USDC-USD. If Pyth stops having the necessary USDC information to resolve this market, a consensus of credible sources for whether USDC was below 98 cents for 24 hours or more may be used to resolve this market.

events_crypto.title: Which companies announce bankruptcy before 2027?
events_crypto.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed company announces that it will file for bankruptcy or has filed for bankruptcy of any variety by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

An announcement will suffice for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of whether or not the actual filing occurs.

The announcement must be made through any of their official or verified channels, including a recorded or written statement by their CEO, legal representation, or any other individual or team that officially represents the company.

A definitive consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

OpenAI:

"OpenAI" refers to OpenAI Group PBC, the company that holds the OpenAI business and is controlled by the OpenAI Foundation, its operating subsidiary OpenAI OpCo, LLC, or any other entity that is controlled by, or is under common control with, OpenAI Group PBC and that holds, directly or indirectly, all or substantially all of OpenAI's business and assets at the time of the filing or announcement. Unless named above, foreign entities, financing entities, special purpose vehicles, and entities used to separate specific legal liabilities will not qualify, even if they meet that test.

A filing for bankruptcy means a petition by an entity this market refers to (each, a "covered entity") under Chapter 7 or Chapter 11 of the United States Bankruptcy Code, or a bankruptcy case for a covered entity filed in a court outside the United States under that country's bankruptcy or insolvency law, including a court-appointed administration. A petition filed against a covered entity by its creditors will qualify only if the court enters an order for relief on that petition by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

An announcement must state that a covered entity has decided to file for bankruptcy, or has filed for bankruptcy. Statements that the company is considering, exploring, or open to bankruptcy, or that bankruptcy is one of several options, will not qualify.

A definitive consensus of credible reporting may be used to confirm that a qualifying announcement or filing occurred. Reports citing unnamed sources that a covered entity plans or is preparing to file will not qualify on their own.

markets.question: Will MicroStrategy announce bankruptcy before 2027?
markets.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the listed company announces that it will file for bankruptcy or has filed for bankruptcy of any variety by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Fully Diluted Valuation of Unit's governance token is greater than the value specified in the title 1 day after launch. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No."

The token must be actively, publicly transferable and tradable to be considered a launch.

The FDV will be determined using the total token supply multiplied by the token price.

"1 day after launch" is defined as 4:00 PM ET on the calendar day following launch. The resolution source for this market is the most liquid price source available. If Unit (https://hyperunit.xyz/) doesn't launch a token by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

events_crypto.title: Printr FDV above ___ one day after launch?
events_crypto.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Fully Diluted Valuation of Printr's token is greater than the value specified in the title 1 day after launch. Otherwise, the market will resolve to "No."

Only an official token launched by Printr will qualify. Stablecoins, memecoins, LSTs and synthetic tokens will not count.

The token must be actively and publicly tradable to be considered a launch.

The FDV will be determined using the total token supply multiplied by the token price.

"1 day after launch" is defined as 4:00 PM ET on the calendar day following launch. The resolution source for this market is the most liquid price source available. If Printr (https://x.com/printr) doesn't launch a token by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "No".

events_crypto.title: Will MicroStrategy announce bankruptcy before 2027?
events_crypto.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if MicroStrategy announces that it will file for bankruptcy or has filed for bankruptcy of any variety by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

An announcement will suffice for a "Yes" resolution, regardless of if or when the actual filing occurs.

The announcement must be made through any of their official or verified channels, as a recorded or written statement by their CEO, legal representation, or other individual or team which officially represents MicroStrategy.

A definitive consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

"MicroStrategy" refers to Strategy Inc (formerly MicroStrategy Incorporated; Nasdaq: MSTR), the parent company of the Strategy group, or any other entity that is controlled by, or is under common control with, Strategy Inc and that holds, directly or indirectly, all or substantially all of MicroStrategy's business and assets at the time of the filing or announcement. Unless named above, foreign entities, financing entities, special purpose vehicles, and entities used to separate specific legal liabilities will not qualify, even if they meet that test.

A filing for bankruptcy means a petition by an entity this market refers to (each, a "covered entity") under Chapter 7 or Chapter 11 of the United States Bankruptcy Code, or a bankruptcy case for a covered entity filed in a court outside the United States under that country's bankruptcy or insolvency law, including a court-appointed administration. A petition filed against a covered entity by its creditors will qualify only if the court enters an order for relief on that petition by December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

An announcement must state that a covered entity has decided to file for bankruptcy, or has filed for bankruptcy. Statements that the company is considering, exploring, or open to bankruptcy, or that bankruptcy is one of several options, will not qualify.

A definitive consensus of credible reporting may be used to confirm that a qualifying announcement or filing occurred. Reports citing unnamed sources that a covered entity plans or is preparing to file will not qualify on their own.

Once a qualifying filing or announcement occurs, this market will resolve to "Yes" even if the petition is later withdrawn, dismissed, or converted, or the company later reverses its decision.

The following will not qualify on their own: a missed payment or other default on debt; a breach of a loan covenant; foreclosure or other enforcement action by creditors; a credit rating downgrade; a debt exchange or other restructuring agreed outside of court; the appointment of a receiver; and an assignment for the benefit of creditors.

If a covered entity stops existing because of a merger or similar transaction, it will no longer be a covered entity. If, after the merger, no covered entity remains, this market will resolve to "No". If the transaction only changes a covered entity's name, state of incorporation, or legal form, or places a new holding company over the same business, the resulting entity will be treated as that covered entity.

A filing occurs at the time recorded by the court. An announcement occurs at the time it is first published by a covered entity or its representative.
